## Epidemiological measures

The 4 cells of a 2×2 table. The third is named `cc` because `c()` is a function.

<table class="twobytwo">
<tr><th></th><th>Disease</th><th>No disease</th><th>Total</th></tr>
<tr><th>Exposed</th><td>a</td><td>b</td><td>a + b</td></tr>
<tr><th>Unexposed</th><td>cc</td><td>d</td><td>cc + d</td></tr>
</table>

| Measure | Formula | Range | Units |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prevalence | cases / population at one point in time | 0 to 1 | none |
| Risk (cumulative incidence) | new cases / at risk at start | 0 to 1 | needs a time period |
| Incidence rate | new cases / person-time | 0 upward | per person-time |
| Risk ratio | `(a/(a+b)) / (cc/(cc+d))` | 0 upward | none |
| Risk difference | `a/(a+b) - cc/(cc+d)` | −1 to 1 | none |
| Odds ratio | `(a*d) / (b*cc)` | 0 upward | none |
| NNT or NNH | `1 / abs(RD)` | 1 upward | needs a time period |
| Attributable fraction, exposed | `(RR - 1) / RR` | up to 1; negative if protective | none |
| Population attributable fraction | `(risk_total - risk_unexposed) / risk_total` | up to 1; negative if protective | none |

```r
a  <- 90; b <- 910; cc <- 30; dd <- 970

risk_exposed   <- a / (a + b)
risk_unexposed <- cc / (cc + dd)

risk_exposed / risk_unexposed            # RR  3.00
risk_exposed - risk_unexposed            # RD  0.06
1 / abs(risk_exposed - risk_unexposed)   # NNH 16.7 (harmful exposure)
(a * dd) / (b * cc)                      # OR  3.20
```

The fourth cell is `dd`, not `d`, because `d` is used below for a dataset.

With confidence intervals:

```r
library(epitools)

# epitools wants the unexposed row first and the non-case column first.
# It does NOT reorder for you; pass rev= if your table is the other way round.
tab <- matrix(c(dd, cc, b, a), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)

riskratio(tab, method = "wald")
oddsratio(tab, method = "wald")
riskratio(tab)$measure     # the estimate and its 95% CI
```

Read the table `epitools` prints back before you trust the number.

## Which measure for which design

| Design | You may compute |
|---|---|
| Cohort | risk, rate, RR, RD, OR |
| Case-control | OR (what it estimates depends on how controls were sampled) |
| Cross-sectional | prevalence, prevalence ratio, prevalence OR |
| Trial | risk, rate, RR, RD, NNT |

## R basics

```r
x <- c(34, 51, 22, 67, 45, 19, 58, NA)   # a vector, with one value missing

length(x); class(x)        # how many, what type

sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)       # 296
mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)      # 42.3
median(x, na.rm = TRUE); sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
min(x, na.rm = TRUE); max(x, na.rm = TRUE); range(x, na.rm = TRUE)

mean(x)                    # NA - one value is unknown, so the mean is unknown
sum(is.na(x))              # 1

sum(x >= 45, na.rm = TRUE)   # 4  - a count
mean(x >= 45, na.rm = TRUE)  # 0.571 - a proportion

round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
```

## Looking at a dataset

```r
nrow(d); ncol(d); dim(d)
names(d)
str(d)
glimpse(d)                 # dplyr
summary(d)
head(d, 10)

table(d$district)
table(d$district, useNA = "ifany")
table(d$exposed, d$disease)
```

## dplyr

```r
library(dplyr)

d |> filter(age >= 50)
d |> filter(age >= 50, sex == "Female")     # comma means AND
d |> filter(district %in% c("Kolar", "Hassan"))

d |> select(id, age, sbp)
d |> select(-dbp)
d |> rename(bp = sbp)

d |> mutate(bmi_cat = if_else(bmi >= 25, "overweight", "normal"))
d |> mutate(band = case_when(
      age < 40 ~ "under 40",
      age < 60 ~ "40-59",
      .default = "60+"
    ))

d |> arrange(age)
d |> arrange(desc(age))

d |> count(district)
d |> count(district, sort = TRUE)

d |>
  group_by(district) |>
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    mean = round(mean(age), 1),
    risk = round(mean(event), 3)
  )
```

`filter()` silently drops rows where the condition is `NA`. Count rows before
and after.

Put `n()` in every `summarise()`.

## ggplot2

```r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(d, aes(x = age, y = sbp)) + geom_point()
ggplot(d, aes(x = sbp)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 10)
ggplot(d, aes(x = district, y = sbp)) + geom_boxplot()
ggplot(d, aes(x = district)) + geom_bar()
ggplot(d, aes(x = district, y = n)) + geom_col()     # when you have the counts
ggplot(d, aes(x = date, y = cases)) + geom_line()
```

Inside `aes()` means the property comes from a column. Outside `aes()` means a
fixed setting.

```r
ggplot(d, aes(x = age, y = sbp, colour = smoker)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ district) +
  labs(title = "...", x = "...", y = "...", colour = "...", caption = "...") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Layers join with `+`, not `|>`.

## Tables for a paper

```r
library(gtsummary)

d |>
  select(age, sex, smoker, sbp, event) |>
  tbl_summary(by = event) |>
  add_p() |>
  add_overall()
```

```r
glm(event ~ smoker + age + sex, data = d, family = binomial) |>
  tbl_regression(exponentiate = TRUE)
```

`exponentiate = TRUE` turns log-odds into odds ratios. Without it the column is
not an OR.

## Keyboard shortcuts in RStudio

| Shortcut | Does |
|---|---|
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> | run the current line |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>M</kbd> | insert the pipe |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> | restart R |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | complete a name |
| <kbd>F1</kbd> on a function | open its help |

On macOS, use <kbd>Cmd</kbd> in place of <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>.

## Getting help inside R

```r
?mean                # help for one function
??"risk ratio"       # search all help
args(round)          # what arguments it takes
sessionInfo()        # your R version and loaded packages
```
